exposure: Umbilical cord coiling index (UCI) (Normocoiled, Hypocoiled, Hypercoiled)
cohort: The participants were pregnant individuals at term gestation whose umbilical cord coiling index was assessed using ultrasonography.
finding: Ultrasonographic evaluation of umbilical cord coiling index (UCI) at term gestation served as an important tool to predict adverse perinatal outcomes, with hypercoiled cords linked to cesarean delivery and low birth weight, and hypocoiled cords to meconium staining, lower Apgar scores, and increased NICU admissions.
mod_finding: Hypercoiled cords were significantly associated with a higher incidence of cesarean delivery.
birth_weight: Low Birth weight was an assessed outcome.
gest_age: The study included pregnancies at term gestation.
